sentences.text: Latirhinus was a medium-sized hadrosaur measuring 8.7 meters long and weighing around 3.75 metric tons.
This duck-billed dinosaur likely lived in groups, featuring a low back and a very broad nose.
The first fossil discovered was a juvenile individual that reached 6 meters in length and weighed an estimated 3 tons.
The genus was named in 2012 based on a partial skeleton found in the Campanian-age Cerro del Pueblo Formation.
A 2012 study determined that the holotype originally defined as a saurolophine was actually a chimera, with the bones belonging to a lambeosaurine.
There are still disagreements among researchers regarding the specific position of Latirhinus within the Lambeosaurinae.
Cladograms show conflicting positions for Latirhinus, with some placing it as a basal lambeosaurine and others as a derived member of Lambeosaurini.
The specific name uitstlani means "southern" in Náhuatl, referencing the species' occurrence in the southern part of the Cretaceous landmass Laramidia.
The time range for Latirhinus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.

Latirhinus lived contemporaneously with Velafrons coahuilensis, Kritosaurus navajovius, Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna, Paraxenisaurus normalensis, and the marine turtle Mexichelys in the Cerro del Pueblo Formation.
